n: A morning prayer. David asks the Lord to listen to his words and even to his unspoken sighs.

f.g: Sighing or groaning — the prayer of the heart beneath the words.

n: He calls God “my King and my God” — the true King above Israel’s earthly king.
Each morning David lays out his prayer like an offering and waits expectantly for God’s answer.

f.g: Arrange or lay out — the same word used for setting out a sacrifice.

n: God takes no pleasure in wickedness; evil cannot live as his guest.

f.w: neither shall evil dwell with thee

n: The arrogant cannot stand before him, and he hates all who practice evil.
He destroys liars and despises the violent and deceitful.
But by God’s great covenant love David may enter his house and bow toward the holy temple in reverence.

f.g: “Mercy” is ḥesed — God’s loyal, covenant love.

n: Because of his enemies, David asks God to lead him and make the way plain before him.

f.w: make thy way straight before my face

n: His enemies can’t be trusted: their hearts are full of destruction, and their throats are like open graves. Paul quotes this to show universal human sinfulness.

f.w: their throat is an open sepulchre

n: David asks God to hold them guilty and let their own schemes bring them down, because they rebel against God.

f.w: let them fall by their own counsels

n: Let everyone who takes refuge in God rejoice and sing forever, because God shelters them.

f.g: Literally “you spread a covering over them.”

n: The Lord blesses the righteous and surrounds them with his favor like a large shield.

f.g: A large body-length shield that covered the whole person.
